Issued at 1145 PM CDT Sun Sep 20 2026

Earlier this evening an upper low that was located over 
Wyoming. An upper level jet was positioned near the base of this
upper level low with scattered convection occurring at this 
time near the nose of this upper jet as it moves east into 
northeast Kansas. At the surface a stationary front extended 
from eastern Colorado into the Panhandle of Texas. Just north of
this boundary a moist upslope flow was present which was aiding
in ongoing nighttime convection as enhanced upper level lift 
develops during the overnight hours as the right entrance region
of the upper level jet moves across western Kansas. Overnight 
scattered elevated thunderstorms are forecast to move southeast 
along the mid level baroclinic zone (700fgen) with improving 
warm air advection and 850-700mb moisture transport occurring. 
As a result the thunderstorms that do move into southwest Kansas
later tonight initially appears to have the potential for hail 
near the Colorado border, but these storms are expected to 
weaken as they cross southwest Kansas. Isolated gusty winds 
along with locally heavy rainfall still will be possible from a 
few of the stronger storms late tonight. CAMS appear in 
reasonably good agreement with these storms crossing southwest 
Kansas between 08z and 16z.


Early morning convection over southwest Kansas will taper 
off/move south of the area by late morning allowing skies to 
clear late day. The upper low that was located over Wyoming 
earlier this evening will now be moving across Nebraska during 
the day on Monday. Given the clearing skies and forecast 
925-850mb temperatures late day it appears that afternoon highs 
will again range from the mid 70s to lower 80s. On Monday 
however the cooler temperatures (mid 70s) will be focused near 
the Colorado border/extreme southwest Kansas given upslope flow,
moisture and linger convection will be present longer in the 
day than further east. 

Ensembles this morning remain in good agreement and consistent 
with previous runs in keeping this cooler air mass which will be
located over southwest Kansas on Monday around through at least
mid week as a cool surface ridge axis builds across the Central
Plains and an upper level ridge starts to move into western 
Kansas from the west. Upper ridge building across western Kansas
early in the week will also limit convection chances to areas 
near and north of the surface boundary which will be located 
across eastern Colorado and the Panhandle of Oklahoma/Texas. 
This would include far western Kansas/extreme southwest Kansas. 

The chance for measurable precipitation will however improve 
mid week as this upper ridge moves east of the area allowing a 
southwesterly flow aloft to return as our next, more 
significant, upper low/trough begins to approach the Central 
Rockies. Several opportunities for widespread accumulating 
rainfall currently is starting to appear more and more likely 
for much of western Kansas starting late Wednesday and 
continuing through the end of the work week as our next upper 
level system weakens as it moves across the Rockies and out into
the plains. IVT has for the past several runs indicated decent 
moisture return to southwest Kansas Wednesday and Thursday as 
southerly winds return on the eastern edge of the upper ridge. 
The latest ensembles all seem to be suggesting PWAT values 
greater than the 95th percentile west of highway 283 from late 
Wednesday through early Friday. This is something that will need
to be monitored closely over the next several days because 
given this environment and possible multiple days of storms 
moving over/near the same areas this could result in some decent
rainfall totals in some locations and possible even some water 
issues late week if these models verify. The latest NBM 48hour 
probability for rainfall totals to exceed 3/4 inches ending at 
7am Friday ranges from 60-80% with the highest rainfall totals 
occurring west/southwest of Dodge City. This is up from a 50-70%
chance of this occurring just 12 hours earlier. Most notable 
item of interest from the past few runs is that the higher 
chances remain unchanged. Also noticing that the EFI and Sot has
also increased over the last 12hour and was starting to 
highlight our extreme western counties. Will be interesting to 
see how persistent these signals will be over few runs. 
Currently HPC during this period only has a Marginal risk for 
our west/southwest but slight risk is as close as the panhandle 
of Oklahoma.
